sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell a house in Deptford?
sections.html:
Deptford owners have three ways out: an agent listing, a private sale, or a straight purchase by a cash buyer. The choice usually follows the condition of the house and the calendar. A tidy house with months to spare suits the open market, while worn systems, tenants, an estate, or a payoff date on the horizon point toward a direct sale.

Deptford Township had an estimated 32,600 residents on July 1, 2025, up from 31,977 at the 2020 count. Delays tend to come from paperwork and repairs, so the sections below cover the township offices, the Gloucester County Clerk, and the state forms that go with every deed.

  • Agent listing: the most exposure, with showings and a buyer who typically needs a mortgage and an appraisal.
  • Private sale: no commission to pay, though pricing, disclosures and the attorney review fall to you.
  • Cash purchase: no showings and no repair list, and the offer reflects the work the buyer inherits.

sections.h2: What should I know about Deptford before I price a house here?
sections.html:
Deptford is a southeastern suburb of Philadelphia, about 10 miles from the city on the New Jersey side of the Walt Whitman Bridge and roughly 50 miles northwest of Atlantic City. Deptford spreads over 17.33 square miles and touches Woodbury, Woodbury Heights, Wenonah, Westville, West Deptford, Washington Township and Mantua Township, with Bellmawr, Runnemede and Gloucester Township across the Camden County line.

The place is old. It was formed in 1695 as Bethlehem and incorporated as a township in 1798. Its best-known story is the 1793 balloon landing at the Clement Oak, the first hot air balloon landing in North America. Most of the housing, though, came with the post-war boom: the population went from about 7,300 in 1950 to nearly 17,900 in 1960 and passed 24,000 by 1970. A lot of the housing stock dates from that boom, which is why roofs, heating systems and wiring draw attention at inspection.

Neighborhood names matter to buyers. Oak Valley, a Census-designated place with about 3,500 residents, lies inside the township, along with the unincorporated communities of Almonesson, Good Intent, Lake Tract, Jericho, Hammond Heights, Westcottville and Woodbury Gardens.

sections.h2: How do Deptford's roads, transit and shopping affect a sale?
sections.html:
Access to Philadelphia is a selling point for Deptford. Routes 41, 42, 45, 47 and 55 all cross the township, and county routes 534, 544, 551 and 553 fill in the grid. The New Jersey Turnpike is reached at Exit 3 in Bellmawr and Runnemede, and a short 0.07-mile piece of Interstate 295 touches the township. NJ Transit buses on the 400, 401, 402, 408, 410 and 412 lines run to Philadelphia, with local service on the 455 and 463.

Deptford Mall, the largest mall in the South Jersey region at about 1.07 million square feet of leasable space, anchors the retail side, with strip malls, restaurants and a movie theater around it. Tall Pines State Preserve, a 111-acre park that opened in November 2015 as Gloucester County's first state park, sits on the border with Mantua Township.

As of 2010 the township had about 150 miles of road: roughly 99 municipal, 29 county, 19 state, and 3.4 under the Turnpike Authority.

One district, Deptford Township Schools, covers the whole township and had 3,942 students in 2020-21. The elementary schools are Good Intent, Lake Tract, Oak Valley and Shady Lane for grades 1 to 5, with Central Early Childhood Center and Pine Acres Early Childhood Center covering the youngest grades. Monongahela Middle School takes grades 6 to 8, and Deptford Township High School takes grades 9 to 12.

County students may also apply to the Gloucester County Institute of Technology, a no-tuition technical high school based in Deptford. Ask the district which of the four elementary schools your street feeds and give that answer to buyers early.

sections.h2: How does Deptford compare on income and housing costs?
sections.html:
Survey estimates for 2020 through 2024 show a township where owners live in roughly three of every four homes and a typical owned home is valued at $277,100.

sections.h2: Does the 2021 tornado still matter when I sell?
sections.html:
It can. An EF3 tornado with winds up to 150 miles per hour, produced by the remnants of Hurricane Ida, struck Deptford on September 1, 2021 and damaged more than 100 homes. A repaired house should have closed permits and passed final inspections on file. One that was patched without permits, or left half-fixed, can stall a mortgage buyer at the inspection or appraisal.

If your house had storm repairs, collect the permit numbers, contractor invoices and insurance papers before you list. The township construction office at 1011 Cooper Street answers questions about open permits and final inspections at (856) 845-5300, weekdays from 8:30 until 4:30. A cash buyer can take unfinished work as it stands, and the offer will account for it.

sections.h2: What local approvals does a Deptford sale need?
sections.html:
The township construction office takes applications for a Housing Certificate of Occupancy. Before signing a contract, ask that office whether your sale needs one and what the inspection covers, since the buyer's attorney is likely to raise it.

Landlords have one more item. The township clerk's page cites N.J.S.A. 46:8-28, which requires rental owners to register with the clerk, and warns of fines reaching $500 for owners who skip it. Selling a tenant-occupied house means checking that your registration is current; the Clerk's Office number is 856-686-2203.

sections.h2: What will closing cost a Deptford seller?
sections.html:
The seller owes the state a realty transfer fee, charged on a sliding scale per $500 of price. Applying the schedule to a $277,100 sale, the Census median for owned homes here, produces roughly $1,536. A $350,000 sale comes to about $2,105, and anything above $350,000 uses a higher schedule.

  • Transfer fee: paid by the seller, with an affidavit (form RTF-1) filed whenever an exemption is claimed.
  • Recording: the Gloucester County Clerk adds a $20 indexing fee when a paper deed shows up without its cover sheet.
  • Seller's tax form: a GIT/REP form signed at closing. New Jersey residents sign the GIT/REP-3 residency certification, and nonresident sellers may owe a prepayment of at least 2 percent of the price.
  • Payoffs: mortgages, liens and unpaid municipal charges are subtracted from your proceeds.

A listing agent's commission is whatever your agreement says, so get the figure in writing before you compare a listing with a cash offer.

sections.h2: Where does the deed go after a Deptford closing?
sections.html:
Deptford deeds are filed with the Gloucester County Clerk. The clerk's land records page requires one of the GIT/REP forms with every deed, and the Record Room answers at 856-853-3230. The county also runs a free Property Fraud Alert that notifies you whenever a document is filed under your name, which is worth setting up after a sale or an inheritance.

For a copy of an older deed, the clerk's page points owners to the online land records search, where one can be printed free, and warns about mailers that charge $75 to $86 for the same document.

sections.h2: When is a direct sale the better fit in Deptford?
sections.html: A direct purchase fits when speed or condition matters more than the final few thousand dollars. In Deptford that might be a parent's house nobody wants to repair, a rental whose tenants are leaving, a property with storm or age damage, or a mortgage slipping behind. Get offers in writing, ask which closing costs the buyer covers, and set the net figure beside your best listing estimate.

faqs.q: Will a Deptford buyer take a house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer takes the property as it stands and prices the work into the offer. A buyer relying on a mortgage may ask for repairs after the inspection or appraisal.

faqs.q: Which office files the deed for a Deptford sale?
faqs.a: The Gloucester County Clerk. The deed has to carry a GIT/REP form, and a paper filing without a cover sheet adds a $20 indexing fee. The Record Room number is 856-853-3230.

faqs.q: What transfer fee would a Deptford seller owe?
faqs.a: It scales with price. On the state schedule, $277,100 produces about $1,536 and $350,000 about $2,105. The seller is responsible for it.

faqs.q: Is there a township inspection before a Deptford sale?
faqs.a: Call the construction office at (856) 845-5300. It handles Housing Certificate of Occupancy applications and can say whether your sale needs one and what gets checked.

faqs.q: Does a rented Deptford house need landlord registration before I sell?
faqs.a: Rental owners register with the township clerk under N.J.S.A. 46:8-28, and the clerk lists fines reaching $500 for skipping it. Make sure yours is current before the buyer's attorney asks.
